description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between computational cost, measured in TFLOPs (trillion floating-point operations) on the x-axis, and the loss ratio (%) on the y-axis, for five different configurations of the SepLLM model compared to a “Vanilla” baseline. The x-axis spans from 1e7 to 9e8 TFLOPs using a logarithmic scale with major ticks at 1e7, 2e7, 5e7, 1e8, 2e8, 3e8, 4e8, 5e8, 6e8, 7e8, 8e8, and 9e8. The y-axis ranges from 94% to 100% loss ratio, with major gridlines every 1% and minor gridlines every 0.2%. The “Vanilla” model (purple line with triangle markers) maintains a near-constant loss ratio of approximately 99.9% across all TFLOP values. The “SepLLM (n=64)” (orange line with square markers) starts at ~98.3% at 1e7 TFLOPs, rises to ~100.2% at 4e8 TFLOPs, then slightly declines to ~99.9% at 9e8 TFLOPs. The “SepLLM (n=128)” (blue line with cross markers) begins at ~97.0% at 1e7 TFLOPs, increases to ~99.9% by 5e7 TFLOPs, and remains stable near 99.9% thereafter. The “SepLLM (n=64, H)” (green line with diamond markers) starts at ~97.5% at 1e7 TFLOPs, rises to ~100.0% by 1e8 TFLOPs, and fluctuates slightly around 100% up to 9e8 TFLOPs. The “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” (red line with circle markers) begins at 94.0% at 1e7 TFLOPs, climbs steeply to ~97.2% at 5e7 TFLOPs, continues rising to ~99.0% at 3e8 TFLOPs, peaks at ~99.2% at 4e8 TFLOPs, then dips to ~98.5% at 5e8 TFLOPs before stabilizing near 98.8% at 9e8 TFLOPs.
